item.description: As QA test automation spreads across an organization, organizing tests and controlling who owns them becomes the real work.

item.description: DAYJOB: Tax is a benchmark that evaluates AI agents across 50 realistic tax environments to test their professional judgment and tax work reliability.

item.title: [news] NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2: Intelligent Multilingual Transcription You Can Prompt and Adapt
[news] Access Multiple AI Models in Your Python Apps Using OpenRouter
item.description: Learn how to get started with the OpenRouter API to call multiple AI models through one API, compare responses, switch models, and set up automatic fallbacks.

item.title: [news] The October inflection point for vibe game development
item.description: I've written before about how November 2025 was an inflection point for coding agents - the point where Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 crossed a tipping point that meant their respective coding agents became reliable daily drivers for software engineers.

item.title: [news] Kentucky man becomes the first humanist granted religious exemption from AI
item.description: Trending on Hacker News from religionnews.com. 350 points and 408 comments.

item.title: [news] OpenAI and ServiceNow expand partnership across enterprise workflows
item.description: OpenAI and ServiceNow expand their partnership to bring OpenAI models and agents into ServiceNow and ServiceNow workflows into ChatGPT and Codex.

item.title: [repo] jmanico/grim-prompter
item.description: Threat modeling tool for AI coding agents that provides architecture workflows and analysis prompts to generate evidence-traced threat models for codebases.

item.title: [news] The future of the firm
item.description: How AI might enter the org chart—beneath, beside, and between us.

item.title: [news] Legora is building the agentic operating system for legal work
item.description: See how Legora uses OpenAI models, ChatGPT, and Codex to accelerate legal workflows, expand contract analysis, and free lawyers to focus on higher-value work.

item.title: [repo] sirioberati/YouTube-AI-Motion-Graphics
item.description: YouTube AI Motion Graphics is an open-source workflow that creates animated HTML explainer boards synced to voice recordings using Whisper, Chrome, and FFmpeg.

item.title: [paper] Quaternion Approximate Networks for Enhanced Image Classification and Oriented Object Detection
item.description: QUAN is a quaternion-based deep learning framework that approximates quaternion convolution with real-valued operations to achieve rotation-equivariant image classification and object detection with improved efficiency.

item.title: [paper] Lipi-Ghor: A Large-Scale, Diarized, Multi-Domain Bengali Speech Corpus and a Scalable Pipeline for Building It
item.description: Lipi-Ghor is a large-scale weakly supervised Bengali speech corpus with speaker-diarized long-form annotations and a gold evaluation split for benchmarking ASR models.

item.title: [paper] Beyond the Estimate: Wiener-Informed Decoding for Easier Training of Pixel-Space Flow Models
item.description: Wiener-informed Decoding accelerates pixel-space velocity model training and improves image generation by integrating statistical predictions into decoder computation without altering native blocks.

item.title: [paper] What Outcome RL Buys: Finishing, Reliability, Rarely Reach
item.description: Reinforcement learning improves pass@1 mainly by finishing answers faster and increasing reliability rather than acquiring new problem-solving knowledge, with minimal reach gains under fixed token budgets.

item.title: [paper] How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning
item.description: Fin-SD improves local multi-step financial reasoning by using self-generated error critiques and truncated correct prefixes for on-policy distillation without external teachers.

item.title: [repo] Speedrunlab/reverse-engineer-anything-self-learning-loop
item.description: Agent skill that examines an authorized product, builds a custom version, and iteratively tests it against a written parity checklist until all requirements pass.

item.title: [repo] Anubis-Security-Tool/anubis
item.description: Open-source cross-platform workspace for cybersecurity research, remote access, system administration, and security automation.

item.title: [tool] ConvFill Gemma Voice Demo
item.description: ConvFill Gemma Voice Demo

item.title: [paper] Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
item.description: Machine learning-enhanced optical modeling of polarized resonant soft X-ray scattering enables quantitative, depth-resolved analysis of molecular orientation and packing at buried interfaces.

item.title: [model] LiquidAI/LFM3-Omni-2B
item.description: Multimodal model from LiquidAI. 714 downloads and 131 likes so far.

item.title: [paper] T-DIG: Text-Conditioned Diversity for Image Generation
item.description: T-DIG is a text-conditioned diversity framework that uses an LLM policy with reinforcement learning to generate axis-specific image variations via frozen generators, enabling user-directed exploration without model retraining.

item.title: [model] LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B
item.description: Vision-language model from LiquidAI. 1.6k downloads and 129 likes so far.

item.title: [paper] AlphaBet: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Event Forecasting Agents
item.description: AlphaBet uses agentic reinforcement learning to train a single LLM policy to search, reason, and report forecast probabilities across multiple dates, reducing Brier scores by improving both evidence acquisition and probability reporting.

item.title: [model] nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B
item.description: Speech recognition model from nvidia. 338 downloads and 137 likes so far.

item.title: [news] Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
[news] Can This Open-Source Model Beat AI Detectors? Let’s Test It Locally
item.description: Can a free, open-source AI humanizer beat paid tools? We tested a 12B model locally and compared the results against AI detectors to see if the hype is real.

item.title: [news] Which Local LMs are Best For Which Tasks
item.description: A local language model is one whose actual weights, the enormous file of learned numbers that constitutes the trained model, you download and run entirely on your own hardware.

item.title: [news] Quoting Terk Terkowitz
item.description: If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing. Document why, share it with your community of peers, bring it to your manager, and work to find solutions.

item.title: [news] Legora is building the agentic operating system for legal work
item.description: See how Legora uses OpenAI models, ChatGPT, and Codex to accelerate legal workflows, expand contract analysis, and free lawyers to focus on higher-value work.

item.title: [repo] harrytted/ai-agent-interview-playbook
item.description: Comprehensive learning and interview preparation manual for AI agent and large language model application engineers, featuring foundational and advanced chapters, practice problems, and Python experiments.

item.title: [repo] davemessew/AgentFlux
item.description: Open-source agentic AI platform that connects documents, data sources, and language models in a visual workflow to automate tasks locally.

item.title: [paper] Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
item.description: EvidenceConnect synthesizes training data to strengthen visual evidence connection, improving spatial perception and multimodal reasoning across diverse tasks.

item.title: [paper] RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions
item.description: RynnWorld-Latent learns cross-embodiment world dynamics via 3D-grounded latent actions, enabling joint pretraining on diverse video sources and synthetic data generation for improved robot policy performance.

item.title: [paper] Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
item.description: Multiscale Policy Optimization improves long-horizon agent training by aligning credit assignment and policy updates at the turn scale.

item.title: [paper] The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data
item.description: Pre-training corpora leave a lexical imprint on zero-shot accuracy that is consistently tracked by word-level unigram cross-entropy across benchmarks, document selection, and prompt routing.

item.title: [repo] siri2moon/moonreel
item.description: MoonReel is an open-source Meta Muse video generator that automates muse.ai to turn an idea into a scripted, subtitled short video for social media platforms.

item.title: [paper] h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
item.description: A simple agentic loop with efficient Lean feedback achieves state-of-the-art formal theorem proving without structured workflows, showing that execution interfaces matter more than complex orchestration.

item.title: [repo] DavidDingXu/hello-llm
item.description: Language model introductory course featuring an interactive small model, 20 illustrated lessons, 23 videos, and browser-based training experiments.

item.title: [repo] vasikmansuri/universal-calling-agent-toolkit
item.description: Universal-calling-agent-toolkit offers provider-neutral telephony adapters, an audio pipeline, and email capture to add reliable voice capabilities to existing AI calling agents.

item.title: [model] openbmb/MiniCPM-OCR-1.0
item.description: Vision-language model from openbmb. 791 downloads and 202 likes so far.

item.title: [paper] Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation
item.description: Looped transformers trained with full backpropagation through time outperform truncated alternatives under matched compute, with scaling laws identifying two loops as optimal when model size is adjustable.

item.title: [repo] aa1143/NamiGPT
item.description: NamiGPT is a beginner-friendly tutorial that builds a GPT-2 model from scratch using PyTorch and loads official OpenAI weights to explain how large language models work.

item.title: [repo] ChannelCooperStart/capri-ai
item.description: Cyberpunk-inspired desktop AI agent that lets users accomplish tasks across their entire Windows machine using popular assistants like Claude Code and Codex.

item.title: [news] Early progress on accelerating drug development with Claude
item.description: Trending on Hacker News from anthropic.com. 190 points and 167 comments.

item.title: [paper] Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
item.description: Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings.

item.title: [paper] ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
item.description: ThinkWorld improves robotic generalization by representing actions as dynamics chains and using world imagination to learn from unlabeled human videos.

item.title: [paper] Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
item.description: Factorized Vector Quantization improves discrete visual token quality by using parallel codebooks on complementary feature views, enabling discrete representations to match continuous ones in multimodal understanding.

item.title: [paper] When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
item.description: Test-time adaptation helps a deployed model respond to changing inputs, but the same intervention can rescue one batch and damage the next. Updating normalization statistics, for example, can improve corrupted images yet fail when a batch contains mostly one class.

item.title: [paper] Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
item.description: We introduce Heads of Security (HoS), a prompt injection defense that enforces instruction-data separation via a small set of learned per-head attention gates.

item.title: [paper] Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
item.description: Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop.

item.title: [paper] KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
item.description: Atmospheric chemical mechanisms are commonly distributed in the language of the Kinetic PreProcessor (KPP), which generates efficient Fortran or C code but does not fit into the differentiable programming frameworks in which machine-learning models are developed.

item.title: [paper] Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
item.description: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands is the next frontier of robotics, yet learned hand skills remain limited to simple grasps or basic repeated motions, such as rotating an object.

item.title: [paper] GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments.

item.title: [paper] Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
item.description: LongChang evaluates whether LLMs can autonomously discover altered physical laws through simulated experimentation, finding that only one model achieved limited success.

item.title: [paper] Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
item.description: We explore how to build performant large language model (LLM) tool-use agents that complete complex, multi-step tasks. Specifically, we study how data composition in synthetically generated tool-use environments affects the training of such agents.

item.title: [paper] MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
item.description: Weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance in language model pretraining, yet a unified understanding of why such control helps and how much is needed remains incomplete.

item.title: [paper] Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
item.description: Self-attention plays a key role in long-sequence modeling, but its quadratic time complexity fundamentally limits the scaling of Large Language Models.

item.title: [paper] Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
item.description: Diffusion language models offer a promising path to efficient agents through parallel token generation. However, efficient interaction requires adapting both where computation is spent and how much text is generated.

item.title: [paper] Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Cross-View Temporal Object Correspondence
item.description: Cross-view object correspondence identifies the same object across views. However, existing methods often rely on frame-wise matching or sequential tracking, which can propagate correspondence errors under appearance changes or occlusions.

item.title: [paper] What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models
item.description: Language models pretrained on web corpora collected over multiple years learn both general and domain-specific knowledge. How these different kinds of knowledge are learned as pretraining progresses remains unclear.

item.title: [paper] Know, then Draw: A New Learning Paradigm for Visual Generation
item.description: Visual generation requires both high-level semantic knowledge and fine-grained pixel details. We propose a learning paradigm that assigns these roles to autoregressive pretraining for knowledge acquisition and diffusion post-training for high-fidelity rendering.

item.title: [paper] Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
item.description: When compressing multi-agent discussions for final decisions, memory selection by rarity or relevance both fail due to decoy inclusion and social-proof bias, and even full transcripts reduce accuracy compared to no notes.

item.title: [paper] Perceiving and Predicting Dynamic Sports: Spatiotemporal Intelligence in Vision Models for Egocentric Tennis Video
item.description: Agile robots require spatiotemporal intelligence to interpret scenes, reason about interactions, and anticipate future events.

item.title: [paper] VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
item.description: Chain-of-thought reasoning has substantially advanced video understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs).

item.title: [paper] Agentic Distributional Regression: Conditional Density Estimation through Agent-Written Programs
item.description: In this paper we propose a method for estimating conditional densities from an iid sample using a language-model agent. The agent writes the estimator as a short program that, for each covariate value, returns the estimated conditional distribution of the response.

item.title: [paper] EnvSched: Environment-Aware Scheduling for Rollout-Efficient Agent Reinforcement Learning
item.description: As executable environments for language agents scale, generating and verifying their rollouts becomes increasingly expensive.

item.title: [paper] Beyond Answer Changes: Matched Same-Class Controls for Local Audio Evidence
item.description: For audio-language models, an answer change after a local sound-event edit can reflect a response to the event's class, sensitivity to waveform rewriting, or both. We compare matched same-class and different-class replacements of a queried event.

item.title: [paper] MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices
item.description: Developing on-device image models requires considering practical user needs, task types and device resource constraints. However, existing benchmarks provide limited guidance on identifying capability gaps between on-device models and server-side models.

item.title: [paper] GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
item.description: Traffic forecasting requires modeling complex temporal dynamics and the spatial dependencies imposed by road topology.

item.title: [paper] Understanding the limits of latent world models
item.description: World models are widely proposed as core components for enabling agents to reason over long temporal and spatial horizons.

item.title: [paper] Timestral
item.description: Timestral is a family of time series foundation models that achieves state-of-the-art probabilistic forecasting through decoupled horizon forecasting, native future covariate support, and synthetic pretraining followed by mixed post-training.

item.title: [paper] REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation
item.description: Personalized recommendation depends on learning semantic and collaborative relations among items from online content and user interactions. Generative recommendation (GR) offers a promising paradigm by autoregressively generating discrete semantic IDs (SIDs) of items.

item.title: [paper] Zero-Shot Multimodal Event Spotting in Soccer Broadcasts
item.description: Automatic soccer event spotting supports highlight generation, video indexing, and sports analytics, but existing methods depend on large annotated datasets and soccer-specific training.

item.title: [paper] Spectral Braids: A Topological Descriptor for Dynamic Directed Networks
item.description: Eigenvalues are a workhorse of graph machine learning: spectral clustering, spectral graph neural networks, and graph kernels all summarize a network by the eigenvalues of a matrix. These eigenvalues are almost always treated as a static list of numbers.

item.title: [paper] As the Story Unfolds: Watching a Film and Identifying Characters as a Human Does
item.description: Films introduce characters incrementally as they progress. We study the problem of identifying principal characters and assigning their names directly from the movie itself, without using external cast lists, actor photographs, or pre-built character banks.

item.title: [paper] The Noise Plane: A Diffusion Bridge Across Exponent and Dispersion
item.description: Diffusion-based denoising commonly uses Gaussian perturbations, whereas sensor noise follows diverse signal-dependent statistical laws. In this paper, we propose $p$-Bridge, a unified measurement-indexed diffusion framework for Tweedie noise.

item.title: [paper] TeamGym: A Gym for Team Decision-Making by AI Agents with Distributed Information
item.description: Many real-world decisions require teams to integrate information distributed across participants. Yet AI agents are still primarily trained and benchmarked in isolation.

item.title: [paper] LCM-Promo: An LLM-Based Uplift Model for Promotion Allocation
item.description: We present LCM-Promo, an LLM-based uplift model for promotion allocation. LCM-Promo is a task-specific Large Commerce Model (LCM): a finetuned LLM trained on transactional commerce data to predict user intent and promotion response.

item.title: [paper] Gym-Anything-RT: Scaling Real-Time Environments for Vision-Language Agents
item.description: AI agents have made substantial progress in domains where they have a non-trivial amount of time to deliberate between actions, such as mathematics, software engineering, and performing tasks on desktop applications.

item.title: [paper] ReferStream: Interactive Subject Injection for Streaming Video Generation
item.description: Injecting new subjects naturally during streaming video generation requires integrating newly supplied visual references into the existing video while preserving established subjects and the scene.

item.title: [paper] Pneuma: A Large-Scale Real-World Time Series Benchmark for Commercial Aircraft Predictive Maintenance
item.description: Predictive maintenance is vital for commercial aviation, yet progress remains hindered by the lack of public, large-scale real-world datasets. As a result, most methods are developed and evaluated on proprietary data, limiting reproducibility.

item.title: [paper] When uncertainty quantification fails: structural vulnerabilities and corrections for selective prediction under clinical class imbalance
item.description: Background. Selective prediction systems improve the safety of clinical artificial intelligence by deferring ambiguous cases to human experts while automating high-confidence decisions.

item.title: [paper] Collective Dynamics of Self-Reinforcement: How Cross-Task Coupling Drives Policy Collapse in Unsupervised RLVR
item.description: Label-free reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) rewards a language model for agreeing with its own majority vote.

item.title: [paper] Kinematic Constraint-Referenced Evaluation for Articulated Object Manipulation
item.description: Manipulation policies are evaluated predominantly by binary task success, which cannot tell whether the commanded gesture is the one the object's kinematics admit.

item.title: [paper] When, Where, and What to Correct: Human-Guided Adaptive Residual Correction for Robot Policies
item.description: Imitation policies that reliably execute most of a manipulation trajectory can still fail in localized regions requiring last-mile precision. Updating the full policy or exploring residual actions everywhere treats this local failure as a global learning problem.

item.title: [paper] GroundControl: Satellite-Conditioned Multi-View Diffusion for Reconstruction-Free Novel View Synthesis
item.description: Multi-view or video diffusion models have recently emerged as state-of-the-art approaches for novel-view synthesis from sparse image collections.

item.title: [paper] Which Hand Was Late? Diagnosis for Robot Failure Recovery in Bimanual Tool Use
item.description: Failure diagnosers for robot manipulation are increasingly vision--language models (VLMs), trained and evaluated on single-arm failures produced by perturbing a successful demonstration.

item.title: [paper] GTFormer: A Syntax-Free Graph Network Alternative to Transformers for 8192$\times$ Length Extrapolation in Linear Time
item.description: Self-attention mechanisms have established the Transformer as the dominant backbone across natural language processing, source code intelligence, and automated theorem proving.

item.title: [paper] The Structure Gap: When More Data Cannot Replace Structured Reasoning
item.description: A persistent belief in modern AI is that sufficiently large learners trained on sufficiently much data can make explicit domain knowledge optional. This paper examines a limitation of that belief.

item.title: [paper] Orthogonal and Parametrized Multi-Attribute Steering of LLMs
item.description: Activation steering offers an effective and efficient way to modify an LLM's behavior at inference time. However, it remains unclear how to apply steering such that the signal is consistently strong and the steering strength has a universally interpretable meaning.

item.title: [paper] A note on data-efficient finetuning of vision foundation models
item.description: Adapting foundation models to a new task within or beyond the training domain is the de facto standard for building specialized machine learning models. Recently, Visual Prompting (VP) has emerged as a promising technique for efficient knowledge transfer.

item.title: [paper] Strategyproof Deep Reinforcement Learning for Online Resource Allocation
item.description: Online resource allocation faces two coupled challenges: (1) allocating scarce resources efficiently under uncertain future demand, and (2) ensuring that agents report task valuations and requirements truthfully (strategyproofness).

item.title: [paper] ALADDIN: Adversarial Latent Diffusion Distillation for One-Step Identity Swapping
item.description: Face swapping transfers a source identity onto a target image while preserving the target's pose, expression, hair, and lighting. The most realistic current methods are diffusion-based, but they need many network evaluations per image.

item.title: [paper] Regression Functions as Fields on Covariate Space: Evolution Equations, the Hessian, and Identification
item.description: For each time $t$, the regression function $m_t(x)=E[Y_t\mid X_t=x]$ of an outcome on contemporaneous covariates can be regarded as a field on covariate space.

item.title: [paper] semanticfa: An R Package for Response-Free Semantic Factor Analysis of Psychometric Scales
item.description: The items of a reflective psychometric scale can be read as a proposal about a construct's structure. Language models make that proposal measurable by converting each item into an embedding, a list of numbers, similar for similar meanings.

item.title: [paper] Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to make and execute decisions that affect living systems. Yet, to our knowledge, ecological reasoning is not a focus of pre- or post-training.

item.title: [paper] From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents
item.description: GUI memory should preserve the results of past actions and learn reusable operations. This is difficult in long-horizon workflows, where agents must use information across applications and useful operations are interleaved with failed attempts.

item.title: [paper] Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
item.description: Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) on instruction data can quietly erode their safety, even when no training example looks harmful. Because this safety-degrading data looks benign, standard content filters struggle to catch it.

item.title: [paper] Keeping Inference in the Radio: Design and Measurement of a Spiking Accelerator for mmWave ISAC Activity Recognition
item.description: Integrated sensing and communication allows wireless networks to recognize human activity from the channel estimates that the receiver computes anyway.

item.title: [paper] HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design
item.description: Designing microbial strains for growth-coupled production, in which cellular growth is linked to the synthesis of a target compound through genetic interventions, is a fundamental goal in metabolic engineering.

item.title: [paper] QD-PINN:A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach to Bayesian Quickest Detection in High-Dimensional Diffusions
item.description: Quickest detection problems (QDPs) arise in a wide range of applications. However, the complementarity structure of the associated variational inequalities poses substantial challenges for traditional numerical methods, particularly in high-dimensional settings.

item.title: [paper] How Reliable Is Individualized Functional-Network Attribution in Resting-State fMRI Cognitive Prediction in ADNI?
item.description: Individualized attribution estimates which functional networks drive a model prediction for a given subject and is often proposed as an interpretable resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) biomarker, but its test-retest reliability is rarely quantified.

item.title: [paper] PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions
item.description: Fine-grained visual perception remains a bottleneck during post-training of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), as perceptual errors can constrain gains from reasoning-focused optimization.

item.title: [paper] Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning
item.description: Medium altitude, long endurance unmanned aerial systems such as Shahed-type strike drones are an unanswered threat in modern conflicts. Conventional air defense systems are too expensive to provide a feasible large-scale solution.

item.title: [news] Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation
item.description: Genie 4: our new world model unlocking unprecedented realism in real-time simulation.

item.title: [paper] What Carries Forward? Pretraining Disclosure Across Language Model Releases
item.description: Understanding how language models were pretrained requires information about their data, processing procedures, and computational resources. However, it remains unclear whether successive releases preserve or expand earlier disclosure.

item.title: [paper] Concordat: Typed Sessions for LLM Agents
item.description: Agents built on large language models are increasingly allowed to take consequential actions: cancelling bookings, issuing refunds, changing accounts.

item.title: [paper] M4Bench: Evaluating Procedural Specification for Clinical EHR Derivation Agents
item.description: Clinical research over electronic health records depends on derived variables whose definitions sit outside the schema, in item codes, time windows, missingness rules, and output-grain choices that change cohorts and downstream conclusions.

item.title: [paper] An Input Skip Can Reparameterize a VAE Without Improving the Generator
item.description: An input skip can reduce reconstruction error while leaving a model's distribution of new samples unchanged.

item.title: [paper] Interpretable Meta-Policies for Neural Decision Making
item.description: Deep Reinforcement Learning remains difficult to interpret and align due to the black-box nature of neural networks.

item.title: [paper] Graph Representation Learning via Adaptive Expectile Aggregation
item.description: Graph neural networks (GNNs) rely critically on neighborhood aggregation, yet conventional mean aggregation may fail to capture class-relevant distributional information, particularly in heterophilic graphs.

item.title: [paper] Test-Time Communication in Trading Agent Swarms
item.description: Communication between agents has mostly been studied on tasks with a shared objective and fast, clear feedback. Trading has neither: each agent manages its own account, with decisions being scored by markets late and noisily.

item.title: [paper] ETAMem: Decoupling and Aligning Heterogeneous Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents
item.description: Long-term memory enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to maintain coherent and personalized interactions across extended conversations.

item.title: [paper] CRISP: Co-designing Pruning and Scheduling for Efficient MoE Inference on Edge Servers
item.description: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference on memory-constrained edge platforms is often dominated by expert-weight movement rather than computation.

item.title: [paper] Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction
item.description: Objective: This study aims to determine whether a hip-exoskeleton policy trained in simulation, by co-adapting with a musculoskeletal human model under a metabolic-energy reward, reduces the metabolic cost of walking in new users without per-user tuning, and how…

item.title: [paper] Representing the Unseen: Rethinking Visual Imagination for Spatial Reasoning
item.description: Visual world models increasingly support spatial reasoning by generating RGB views of unobserved states.

item.title: [paper] FeatureArc: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Evolving Features
item.description: A software feature usually evolves over time: developers extend its first version as new use cases and requirements arrive, and each extension builds on code written earlier. Most feature benchmarks evaluate a single request on a fixed codebase.

item.title: [paper] Segmentation Confidence for Arbitrary CNNs
item.description: Convolutional neural networks (CNN) are widely used for medical image segmentation. However, they lack an inherent measure of confidence.

item.title: [paper] When Visual Evidence Is Insufficient: How Instructions, Post-Training, and Internal Activations Shape Refusal in Multimodal Language Models
item.description: For reliable deployment, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) should recognize when an image provides insufficient evidence to answer a question and withhold unsupported answers.

item.title: [paper] Bayes-Adaptive MDPs for Rollout Allocation to Enhance GRPO Training
item.description: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has demonstrated strong performance in LLM post-training. However, it allocates a uniform rollout budget to every training question, ignoring variations in question difficulty.

item.title: [paper] Beyond the Readout: A Latent Numerical Frame Shared Across Modality and Operation
item.description: When a multimodal model computes 17+35 from text or 91-39 from a rendered image, it produces the same answer, 52. Does it use one internal concept of number for both, or separate machinery for each path? Similarity metrics such as RSA or CKA cannot settle this question.

item.title: [paper] Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling
item.description: Brownian stochastic interpolants connect paired endpoint samples, yet their sampling error can depend on displacement moments even when neither endpoint has a first moment.

item.title: [paper] Can Complementary Signals Bridge Similarity Islands? Manifold-Augmented Graph Embedding for Multimodal Recommendation
item.description: Multimodal Recommender Systems (MMRS) leverage rich item features to mitigate data sparsity, yet similarity-driven graph construction and propagation can favor semantically similar substitutes over functionally related complements.

item.title: [paper] Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution
item.description: Agentic Entity Resolution (ER) systems iteratively plan actions, retrieve evidence, revise hypotheses, and propose graph mutations. An erroneous identity hypothesis may condition later retrieval and produce apparent confirmation.

item.title: [paper] CTBakeGS: training-free baking of photorealistic CT volume renderings into 3D Gaussian splats
item.description: Photorealistic volume rendering of computed tomography (CT) may convey anatomy intuitively, but it needs the CT data, dedicated software and a powerful graphics processor.

item.title: [paper] Clearing the FoG: Training KG Agents to Retrieve the Evidence Behind Their Answers
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) can answer many factual questions correctly, but a correct answer is not necessarily a supported one.

item.title: [paper] An end-to-end framework for uncertainty-aware validation of generative models
item.description: Density estimation with generative models is a common task in the physical sciences, for example in background estimation in particle physics. Existing machine learning techniques, however, lack methods to quantify uncertainties that can be propagated into a statistical test.

item.title: [paper] Game-Theoretic Solvers with Bayesian Opponent Modeling and Moral Rhetoric Framing for GLEE
item.description: We describe the agent we submitted to the GLEE Competition, which plays bargaining, negotiation, and persuasion games against a shared pool of human and AI opponents.

item.title: [paper] Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling
item.description: Robot policy evaluation often relies on a binary success signal for task completion.

item.title: [paper] JEPA-Inspired Latent Field Prediction for Sparse-Pilot MIMO-OFDM Channel Reconstruction
item.description: Accurate acquisition of full channel state information (CSI) is essential for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) wireless systems, while dense pilot-based estimation incurs substantial overhead.

item.title: [paper] LinMix: Data Mixing as Linear Domain Attribution
item.description: Language model performance depends strongly on the mixture of domains in the pretraining data corpus.

item.title: [paper] How Many and How Much? Contrastive Learning with Negative Samples for Knowledge Graph Embedding
item.description: Knowledge graph embedding (KGE), a fundamental technique for knowledge-centric Web and KG-augmented AI applications, is commonly trained through contrastive learning with negative samples to learn discriminative representations.

item.title: [paper] Para-Gaussian Approximations of Random Deep Neural Networks
item.description: It is known that randomly initialized neural networks have Gaussian behaviour in the $n\to \infty$ limit. Unfortunately, this approximation can be poor for finite $n$ and gets worse as one goes deeper into the network.

item.title: [paper] Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data
item.description: Prox replaces calibrated thresholds with top-k channel selection and a weight-derived reader to accelerate Mixture-of-Experts inference while preserving accuracy.

item.title: [paper] PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
item.description: PDRVLA improves robot action generation by integrating a lightweight physical dynamics module that predicts future visual features with world-model supervision, avoiding online video generation latency.

item.title: [paper] Same Verdict, Different Readers: Personalizing Fact-Checking Explanations from Relative Preferences
item.description: Fact-checking explanations help Web users understand why a claim receives its verdict, yet the same explanation may not satisfy readers with different backgrounds and preferences.

item.title: [paper] Agent-Conditioned Routing: Diverse Reasoning Paths Within One Frozen Model
item.description: Generating several solutions can expose alternative methods, but additional trajectories often paraphrase one dominant approach.

item.title: [paper] Euclidean Crowding-Driven Adaptive Euclidean-Hyperbolic Graph Learning
item.description: Hyperbolic graph representation learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for modeling hierarchical data.

item.title: [paper] The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models
item.description: Deep learning algorithms have become widely used and successful across a wide range of tasks. A key challenge is determining whether these algorithms truly capture the intrinsic geometry of their training data in order to better understand what they learn from data.

item.title: [paper] Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are usually evaluated by final-output correctness or safety, yet an endpoint label does not reveal how a failure develops throughout the reasoning process.

item.title: [paper] TRIDENT-Seq: Profile-Matched Prefix-Future Contrast for Label-Efficient Payment Risk Modeling
item.description: Ant International accumulates large volumes of transaction history across users and payment businesses. Confirmed fraud and chargeback outcomes, by contrast, are scarce, delayed, and specific to each business.

item.title: [paper] EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
item.description: EmbeddingGemma 2 is an open multimodal embedding model that unifies text, images, audio, and video representations with efficient resource-flexible design and state-of-the-art benchmark performance.

item.title: [news] Retell uses OpenAI models to help power 100M monthly calls
item.description: GPT-6 Astra tops Retell’s voice agent benchmark, while Codex helps it reach a $1.6M annual revenue run rate per employee.

item.title: [paper] Online Interval Selection with Binary Predictions: Optimal Consistency and a Continuous Robustness Tradeoff
item.description: We study online interval selection with binary predictions of membership in a final optimal solution. Requests arrive in arbitrary order; accepted requests may be revoked, but rejected or revoked requests cannot be recovered.
